**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.**

options.text: A result that is still unclear and can go either way
When you are mistreated the same way you mistreat others
A visual presentation is far more descriptive than words

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"When you are mistreated the same way you mistreat others."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**a taste of his own medicine"** means to experience the same negative treatment that one has inflicted on others. (कठोर या अप्रिय व्यवहार जो किसी व्यक्ति द्वारा अन्य लोगों के साथ किए गए व्यवहार जैसा है)

 
 
• **Example**: *The movie is about a playboy who gets a **taste of his own medicine**__ when the girl he falls in love with jilts him for another guy.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is suggesting that the bully should be treated in the same way that he has treated others.
 
• This idiom is often used to convey a sense of justice or comeuppance.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

questions.question:
**Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error.'**

In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg, / and me works on my short / game with a baseball glove.

options.text: and me works on my short
In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg,

questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"and me works on my short."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject pronoun **"me"** is incorrect in this sentence as it should be the object pronoun **"I."**
 
• **"I"** is the subject of a sentence, while **"me"** is the object, meaning that we should use **"I"** if you are the one acting, while **"me"** is the word to use when an action is done to us.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• ***I**__ ate the fish. *
 
• *The fish ate __**me**__.*
 
 
 
• The correct sentence should be *"In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg, __**and I work on my short**__ game with a baseball glove."*
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:
**Direction: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

These were two Indian men who ______ hiding in the forest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"had been."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in past tense, so the correct option should also be in past tense.
 
• **"Had been"** is the correct past perfect continuous tense form of the verb **"to be".**
 
• We use the **past perfect continuous** to talk about actions or events which started before a particular time in the past and were still in progress up to that time in the past.
 
 
• **Example**: *I **had been working**__ on my essays the night before and I was very tired.*
 
 
 
• The use of **"hiding"** suggests that the men were doing something in secret, which makes the past perfect tense appropriate.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

**Correct sentence**: *These were two Indian men who __**had been**__ hiding in the forest. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 - "was"** is in the past tense, but it is not the correct form of the verb "to be" in this context.
 
• **Option 2 - "has been"** is in the present perfect tense, which is not appropriate for a sentence in the past tense.
 
• **Option 4 - "have being"** is not grammatically correct. It should be "have been".
